mechanism_narrative: The sustained increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last three weeks indicates a continuing recovery trend, which will persist over the next four weeks as consumer confidence grows.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week surge in PARKS mobility at t-0w suggests a strong increase in outdoor activity and willingness to leave home, acting as a leading indicator for increased discretionary retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 10 points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase, or PARKS mobility declines sharply in the subsequent week, invalidating its leading indicator status.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility and increasing TRANSIT mobility signifies a fundamental shift away from home-bound activities towards commuting and leisure, directly boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL decreases while TRANSIT increases for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases while TRANSIT mobility decreases over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite these trends.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent, albeit slow, increase in WORKPLACES mobility over the last four weeks indicates a gradual return to offices, which will steadily drive increased demand for retail and recreation services near workplaces over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility plateaus or declines over the next four weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not increase, suggesting no linkage between office return and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: The steady increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, now exceeding -20% from baseline, indicates a recovery in essential out-of-home activity that will precede and enable a rise in discretionary retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds -20% from baseline at t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility falls below -20% again within the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous recovery across RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, and the decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a broad-based societal shift towards increased activity outside the home, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: A majority of the out-of-home categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS) decline, or RESIDENTIAL increases, indicating a reversal of the broad recovery trend.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past two weeks signifies a sustained behavioral shift away from staying at home, directly correlating with increased out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, over the next week.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases week-on-week at t+1w, or RETAIL_REC declines, indicating a reversal of the behavioral shift.

mechanism_narrative: The steady increase in TRANSIT mobility, showing positive week-on-week changes for two consecutive weeks, suggests an easing of restrictions or increased confidence in public transport, which will facilitate higher RETAIL_REC in Manhattan over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT mobility shows a positive week-on-week change for at least two consecutive weeks at t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility declines or plateaus in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not improve, indicating that transit recovery is not driving retail activity.
